To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the scalar radiation from rotating black holes is anisotropic, and that the anisotropy is a function of the black hole angular momentum, the brane tension, and the brane scalar field mass.

the emission of a scalar field from rotating brane black holes is not anisotropic in general and that the angular distribution of emitted quanta depends on the spin of the field and on the black hole angular momentum.

(i) the Hawking temperature for a rotating black hole is the same as that for the corresponding Schwarzschild black hole, (ii) the emission rates are proportional to the angular velocity of the brane and (iii) there are no angular momentum or spin-dependent corrections in the low frequency limit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of Hawking radiation from rotating brane-localized fields in a five dimensional space-time.
the study of Hawking radiation from rotating black holes at future collider experiments.
the Hawking radiation of a rotating brane black hole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are two types of Hawking radiation from rotating black holes: one is the usual Hawking radiation, the other is the anisotropic Hawking radiation.
the Hawking radiation of a brane field from a rotating black hole is anisotropic and its intensity is proportional to the angular momentum of the black hole.
the scalar field emission from rotating black holes is anisotropic, and that the anisotropy is stronger for higher dimensional black holes and/or higher spin brane fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have obtained the complete expressions for the Hawking radiation rate of brane-localized fields in terms of the black hole parameters, the brane field properties, the brane tension, the brane curvature, and the brane coupling.
the scalar field emission from the rotating black holes is anisotropic, and the anisotropy is more pronounced for higher dimensional black holes, and the angular momentum of black holes.
we have obtained the complete expressions for the Hawking fluxes of the scalar field in the high frequency regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scalar field emission from a rotating black hole is anisotropic and the anisotropy is more pronounced in higher dimensions.
the anisotropic character of the Hawking radiation for rotating black holes leads to a significant suppression of the scalar emission.
the anisotropic Hawking fluxes from rotating black holes are significantly larger than that from their non-rotating counterparts.
